- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day horizon — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the first 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model overreacts and forecasts a prolonged overshoot — cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >75, reduce by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes below 70.
- Model lags in capturing short-term reversals — if true outcome drops below 65 after 5+ days of rising, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day.
- Forecast tends to be too smooth — if true outcome shows volatility (e.g., ±5% swings), add ±1–2% noise to forecast to match observed volatility.
